title: Hackers Abuse Windows Mshta.exe in Phishing Attacks to Deploy HTA Malware and Steal Credentials
content_md: Threat actors are actively abusing the legitimate Windows utility mshta.exe to execute malicious HTML Application (HTA) files delivered through Spanish-language phishing emails, enabling system reconnaissance and the staged deployment of credential-stealing malware. Researchers at Fortra’s Intelligence and Research Experts (FIRE) have tracked the campaign since June. It primarily targets Spanish-speaking users at global organizations through fake invoice and judicial-notice lures, including emails titled around Facturación and Aviso Judicial . The messages originate largely from accounts hosted by Italian provider libero.it, using italiaonline.it infrastructure. A notable element of the campaign is the apparent abuse of an email spam-confidence-level bypass. Hackers Abuse Windows Mshta.exe in Phishing Attacks Messages categorized as high-confidence phishing reportedly received an SCL:-1 value, allowing them to reach recipients’ inboxes rather than being quarantined by Microsoft email defenses. The attack begins when a victim clicks a shortened URL embedded in the phishing email. The links redirect through services including goo[.]su , abrir[.]link , and abre[.]ai before leading to a malicious delivery page hosted through archivogratuito[.]online . Victims are ultimately prompted to open an HTA file, such as Doc_02º.HTA . When launched, the file is handled by mshta.exe , a signed Microsoft binary designed to execute HTML Applications.
